title: TracePoint digest
description: The agent-facing view of a run: a prioritised summary small enough to read in full inside a context window. Read it top to bottom and stop when you have your answer - the order is the priority order. Check validity first, because an invalid run measured the load generator rather than the target and must not be interpreted. Field names carry their units (p99_ms, error_ratio, achieved_rps); numbers are numbers, never strings; there is no ANSI and no filler prose. When content had to be dropped to fit a character budget, truncated is true and more says how to fetch the rest.

schema_version.description: Version of this document's shape, MAJOR.MINOR.

run_name.description: Human label given to the run, when one was set.

status.description: How the run ended. Anything other than completed means the data is partial.

duration_s.description: Load duration in seconds, excluding drain.

validity.description: Whether the run can be believed. Read this before the verdict. valid: the generator kept up and nothing undermines the numbers. degraded: usable, with the stated caveat attached to any conclusion. invalid: the generator, not the target, set the pace - the verdict below must not be quoted, and the fix is in the findings.

findings.description: Why it is not valid, each with the change that would fix it.

caveats.description: What the configuration could not see or was warned about before the run - such as a database probe that touches no table - so a clean result is not read as more than it proves. Added in 1.1.

slo.description: Budget outcome. pass false is why the command exited 1.

pass.description: True when every configured budget held. True with no budgets configured means nothing was checked, not that the system is healthy.

configured.description: Whether any budget was configured at all.

budget.description: Configured limit: milliseconds for latency, a ratio for error_rate.

actual.description: Measured value in the same unit.

verdict.description: Which tier the latency came from, with the evidence behind it. This is an association observed on a shared clock, not a proof of causation; the caveat field says so and should be carried into any report built from this.

bottleneck.description: app: the application tier itself. db or redis: that storage tier. client: the load generator or its configuration, not the target. none: nothing stood out. inconclusive: the data cannot say.

confidence.description: From sample sizes, incident count, correlation strength and whether server-side telemetry corroborated it. Do not report a low-confidence verdict as a finding.

summary.description: One paragraph, safe to quote verbatim.

evidence.description: The specific observations behind it, each checkable in result.json.

caveat.description: The standing limitation of the method.
examples: Shared-clock correlation shows association, not causation.

next_steps.description: What to do next, in priority order.

incidents.description: The most significant episodes, worst first. The full list is in result.json and through get_run_section.

class.description: correlated: app and a storage tier were hot together. storage_only: a storage tier was hot while users were unaffected - a bottleneck not yet visible. app_only: the app was hot while every probe stayed healthy. client_limited: the generator's own waiting dominated, so this says nothing about the target. unobserved: too little probe data to classify.

culprit.description: Best-ranked tier, or null when none stands out or several tie.

app_p99_ms.description: Worst application p99 during the episode.

culprit_p99_ms.description: Worst p99 of the implicated tier.

lead_buckets.description: How many buckets the culprit went hot before the application did.

corroboration.description: Server-side signals that moved in the same window.

runners.description: Headline numbers per tier over the measured window, warm-up excluded. Latency is response time - what a user feels.

kind.description: app is the tier users talk to; storage is a probe-and-load tier behind it.

service_p99_ms.description: Service time p99 - what the target did, with generator-side waiting removed.

client_wait_p99_ms.description: Generator-side waiting at p99. When this is a large share of p99_ms, the number describes the generator, not the target.

dropped_ratio.description: Share of scheduled arrivals never dispatched for want of a worker.

top_errors.description: The most common failure classes, worst first.

correlation.description: How closely each storage probe's latency tracked the application's over the whole run. A positive lag means the storage tier moved first.

rho.description: Spearman rank correlation at the best lag, -1 to 1.

lag_buckets.description: Lag maximising the correlation, in buckets.

n_buckets.description: Buckets compared. Below about 30 this is weak evidence.

telemetry.description: One line per sampler: what it saw, or why it saw nothing. An unavailable sampler lowers verdict confidence.

reason.description: Why it was unavailable, and the grant that would fix it.

last_ok.description: Highest level that held every budget.

stable.description: False when re-running the boundary flipped it, in which case quote the range, not a number.

usl.description: Scalability fit, present only when it was reliable enough to report.

strain.description: For ramping runs, where latency started to degrade.

next_window.description: The range a follow-up capacity search should cover, in the knob's units. Added in 1.1.

recommendations.description: What to do next, machine-applicable. An entry with action rerun can be executed directly: `tracepoint run --from <run_id>` plus one --set per override. Apply one at a time and compare, so that a change can be attributed.

why.description: The observation that prompted it, with numbers.
examples: client_wait dominated 7 hot buckets; Little's Law needs ~240 in flight

action.description: rerun: re-run with the overrides given. configure: change the target's configuration, not the test. investigate: look at something outside TracePoint's view.

overrides.description: For action rerun, the exact --set arguments to apply.

artifacts.description: Where the full data lives when the digest is not enough.

report.description: The offline HTML report, for a human.

truncated.description: True when content was dropped to fit the character budget. What remains is still the highest-priority material.

more.description: How to get what was left out.

examples: tracepoint digest <run-id> --budget-chars 16000, or get_run_section for one section at a time
